## Purpose and Entry Points
Anki is the desktop spaced-repetition application. Its primary runtime is a Python/Qt desktop client backed by Rust domain logic and SQLite storage. Desktop startup is packaged through `qt/runanki.py` and `qt/installer/app/src/anki/__main__.py`; the Qt application shell is centered in `qt/aqt/main.py`.

## Desktop Presentation Layer
The `aqt` Python package owns native Qt windows, user interaction, profiles, background tasks, and add-on integration. It orchestrates domain calls rather than implementing most collection logic. Key surfaces include study/review (`qt/aqt/reviewer.py`), card browsing (`qt/aqt/browser/browser.py`), and note editing (`qt/aqt/editor.py`). Web content is embedded in Qt WebViews and locally served media (`qt/aqt/webview.py`, `qt/aqt/mediasrv.py`).

## Rust Collection Core and Persistence
`rslib` is the authoritative domain layer: collections, notes, cards, decks, notetypes, undo, imports, search, scheduling, statistics, and sync. `rslib/src/collection/mod.rs` establishes collection lifecycle and transactional behavior; domain services expose operations around it. Storage is SQLite-oriented, with schema/migrations and SQL-backed repositories under `rslib/src/storage/sqlite.rs`, `rslib/src/storage/schema11.sql`, and `rslib/src/storage/upgrades/`.

## Cross-Language API Boundary
Python calls Rust through generated protobuf-oriented backend APIs, not by directly owning core business rules. The public contract begins in `proto/anki/backend.proto`; Rust request handlers are grouped in `rslib/src/backend/mod.rs`; Python bridge/client code is in `pylib/anki/_backend.py` and `pylib/anki/rsbackend.py`. `pylib/rsbridge/lib.rs` provides the native Rust/Python bridge. This is the critical compatibility boundary for the desktop UI, Python library, and add-ons.

## Study, Rendering, and Web UI Flow
A review action flows from Qt or TypeScript UI through the bridge to Rust scheduling, which selects/answers cards, writes card/review-log changes transactionally, and returns state/rendering data. Scheduling and FSRS behavior reside in `rslib/src/scheduler/mod.rs`, `rslib/src/scheduler/answering/mod.rs`, and `rslib/src/scheduler/fsrs/mod.rs`. Card-template rendering is in `rslib/src/card_rendering/service.rs`. Modern embedded UI is Svelte/TypeScript: reviewer code is `ts/reviewer/index.ts`; routed screens such as editor and deck options are in `ts/routes/editor/+page.svelte` and `ts/routes/deck-options/[deckId]/+page.svelte`.

## Sync and External Integrations
Collection and media sync use HTTP protocol clients against AnkiWeb-compatible services, with optional server runtime. Client sync logic is in `rslib/src/sync/collection/mod.rs` and `rslib/src/sync/media/syncer.rs`; HTTP transport is `rslib/src/sync/http_client/mod.rs`. The standalone sync server binary starts at `rslib/sync/main.rs`, with server routes/handlers under `rslib/src/sync/http_server/`. Separate integrations include AnkiHub (`rslib/src/ankihub/mod.rs`) and AnkiDroid services (`rslib/src/ankidroid/service.rs`).

## Build, Generated Contracts, and Distribution
This is a multi-runtime build: Rust, Python, Qt 6, Node/TypeScript/Svelte, protobuf, Sass, and platform packaging. Rust build configuration generates Ninja workflows from `build/configure/src/main.rs` and `build/ninja_gen/src/lib.rs`. Protobuf definitions in `proto/anki/` generate language bindings; Fluent localization sources in `ftl/core/` are compiled/consumed by Rust and frontend layers. Release packaging targets Windows, macOS, and Linux via `qt/installer/`, while CI/release automation runs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`.
